# Chieftain (01, engineer) — BAD-067

## Brief
`itest('/otp short-circuits the reviewer address without erroring')` in
`test/server/functions.test.mjs:1449` asserts 200. On a long-lived local stack it
returns 429 once the suite has run six times inside one hour, and the failure
reads as a broken test in whatever branch happens to be the sixth run. It cost two
spudagents on BAD-047 an explanation apiece.

Why: `server/supabase/functions/otp/index.ts:49` limits `otp:${email}` to 5 per
3600s. Every other address the suite uses carries a per-run suffix
(`buyer+ord_<ts>@example.com`, `stranger+u_<ts>@example.com`) and the IP buckets
are run-scoped too (`RUN_IP`, `functions.test.mjs:101`), so those reset each run.
`REVIEWER_EMAIL` does not: it is the fixed constant `reviewer@badtakes.io`
(`functions.test.mjs:67`), so its bucket accumulates across runs and the sixth
one trips it. Observed on the BAD-047 worktree stack: `private.rate_limits` held
`otp:reviewer@badtakes.io` at count 7 in a window opened at 00:17 while every
per-run bucket sat at 1 or 3.

Not a CI problem — a runner builds a fresh stack per run, so the counter starts at
zero and one run charges it once. Purely a local re-run papercut.

One option is already narrowed for you, so do not spend the turn on it: the test
cannot randomize the address the way the buyer and stranger fixtures do.
`REVIEWER_EMAIL` is read by the *server* from its own environment (see
`server/supabase/.env.example` and `.env.local`), and the test's constant only
mirrors it — the comment at `functions.test.mjs:64` says so explicitly. An address
the test invents matches nothing on the server, the short-circuit never fires, and
the test stops proving the thing it is named for. So the real choice is between
owning the bucket in the suite's setup (the way a test that owns its fixture
would) and changing what the limit is keyed on.

Judgement is the point of this ticket, and it is yours: decide which, say why in
your Result, and implement it. Two things to weigh.

First, the rate limits on `/otp` are load-bearing in production — accounts are
free, so they are the only thing between that endpoint and a stranger using it to
send mail (the head comment in `otp/index.ts` and `server/README.md`'s
cf-connecting-ip pre-launch note both say so). A fix that weakens or reshapes the
production limit to make a test pass is the wrong fix. A fix confined to the test
suite is strongly preferred; if you conclude the production key genuinely should
change, that is a `proposal file`, not something you do here.

Second, `/otp` is not the only shared bucket on this address. `activate:${email}`
at 20/hour is keyed the same way, and the comment at `functions.test.mjs:1429`
deliberately accepts that sharing. Whatever you do for `/otp`, say in your Result
whether the same reasoning applies to the activate bucket and whether it should be
covered here or left alone — and if the clean fix covers both at once, take it.
Whatever you leave alone, leave that comment telling the truth: if it still says
"many more than that inside an hour reads as 429s here, not a regression" while
the OTP bucket no longer behaves that way, fix the comment too.

Whatever you write must keep the suite's two standing properties: it skips cleanly
with no local stack (CI depends on that — see the `itest` helper and the stack
probe above it), and a run leaves the stack in a state the next run can use. If
your fix reaches into `private.rate_limits` through the service key, it belongs
next to the other setup the suite already does, with a comment saying why the test
owns that row.
